That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.
68	
69	## The worldgen hash policy
70	
71	Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.
72	
73	**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**
74	
75	Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.
76	
77	To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.
78	
79	The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).
80	
81	The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.
82	
83	The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.
84	
85	The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.
86	
87	## Writing new tests
88	
89	- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
90	- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
91	- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
92	- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

# Testing

Two runners, three layers:

- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.

## Running the E2E suite

```bash
bunx playwright install chromium   # once
bun run test:e2e                   # builds and starts the prod server itself
```

E2E tests assert through `window.__monecraft` (the live engine/renderer/input handle — also handy in the browser console) instead of pixels; the one render check uses `renderer.renderedTriangles()`. The shared `gamePage` fixture seeds a default profile + world and enters it through the menu (reloads auto-resume the tab's world), then fails any test that logs a console error; `menu.e2e.ts` instead drives the menus from empty storage with the plain Playwright `test`.

**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.

**happy-dom has no `AudioContext`** (and the `zzfx` package instantiates one at import): everything above the `SynthBackend` seam is pure and tested with a recording fake (see `audioDirector.test.ts`); the WebAudio glue itself (`synth.ts`, `musicPlayer.ts`, `rainLoop.ts`) plus real synthesis quality belong to the manual gameplay pass.

**Known limitation:** headless Chromium cannot engage pointer lock (`requestPointerLock` never resolves). `acquirePointerLock` in `e2e/helpers.ts` tries the real thing, then falls back to forcing the input controller's lock flag — so key/mouse → engine wiring is still tested end to end, but real lock acquisition and look-around feel remain in the manual gameplay pass, along with visual quality. That manual pass is now only required for changes to pointer-lock handling or visual appearance.

## The worldgen hash policy

Saves store only the world seed plus block-change deltas, so `generateWorld` must produce byte-identical output for a given seed forever. The digests in `generation.test.ts` enforce that.

**If a hash test fails after your change, your change breaks every existing save. Fix the code, never the hash.**

Re-baselining the digests is legitimate in exactly one case: a **deliberate worldgen change** — flag it in the PR and CHANGELOG, and bump `WORLDGEN_VERSION` so affected worlds discard their stale block-diffs (rebooting from their seed) rather than corrupting.

To regenerate digests: temporarily log the computed hash in the failing test, run `bun test`, and paste the new values into `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` in the same commit as the cause.

The digests are also an **engine-portability contract**: since worldgen v11, every seed-determined noise call uses the bit-portable implementations in `lib/world/noise.ts` (polynomial sine, integer hashes — only IEEE-exact operations), so the same seed generates identical bytes on every JS engine. `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts` proves it in CI by recomputing the full-size world digest inside Chromium/V8 and asserting it equals the Bun/JSC baseline in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts` — this is what lets a browser client and a multiplayer Bun server share worlds by seed + block diff. `lib/world/noise.test.ts` additionally pins exact golden doubles of the noise primitives. New worldgen code must import its noise/trig from `lib/world/noise.ts`, never `Math.sin`/`Math.cos` (engine-defined per ECMA-262 — the reason the old digests were only valid on a pinned Bun).

The **portable-noise worldgen (v10 → v11)** is the most recent legitimate re-baseline: same wave formulas on `portableSin`/`portableCos`, plus an integer-hash `hash2D`. All seven digests re-rolled; **every structural probe passed unchanged** — the polynomial sine tracks the real one within ~6e-8, so terrain structure is preserved and only scattered single-block flips (cobble speckle, cave edges, flora patterns) moved the hashes. This bump also retired the old "case 2" (a Bun version bump could shift `Math.sin` results): the CI Bun pin is no longer load-bearing for worldgen, though it stays pinned for plain reproducibility.

The **deep-cave lava worldgen** was the prior re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v6 → v7. As with dungeons the structural probes (surface heights/biomes/snow/water) were left unchanged on purpose — `placeLava` runs after `placeOres` so it can't shift the ore→tree RNG stream, and the lava sits at or below `lavaLevel`, so the surface is byte-identical. A probe asserts lava is present and never rises above `lavaLevel`. Note the per-voxel **lighting** change re-rolled nothing: light is a derived runtime cache, never part of the generated bytes, and the meshing snapshot hashes only vertex positions — the new `aLight` attribute leaves them untouched.

The **0.7.0 dungeon worldgen** was an earlier re-baseline: the four worldgen digests and the in-region meshing snapshot were re-rolled and `SAVE_KEY` bumped v5 → v6. The structural probes were left unchanged — dungeons are wholly underground, so the surface bytes are identical.

## Writing new tests

- Pure logic (inventory, spawn rules, a new system): unit-test the module directly.
- Gameplay behavior: boot a small engine — `new GameEngine({ seed, rng, worldSize: { x: 64, y: 150, z: 64 } })` — and step it with synthetic `FrameInput`. Inject a seeded `rng` (see `mulberry32` in the engine tests) for determinism.
- The world boots at dawn with hostiles nearby; use the `calmDaytime` pattern from the engine tests when testing unrelated mechanics.
- A ray origin exactly on a voxel boundary may target a diagonal neighbor (DDA ambiguity) — center positions in cells when aiming at specific blocks.

**happy-dom has no 2D canvas context**: generated sprites degrade to a transparent data URL in component tests — assert sprite pixels in the pure `lib/ui` tests and component structure via roles/labels/`data-icon` attributes, not image sources.

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.
4	
5	## [Unreleased]
6	
7	### Added
8	
9	- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket — protocol v1 (JSON envelopes + one gzipped world-sync frame; total validation of hostile input with a per-command allow-list), 20 Hz fixed-tick rooms with client-pose clamping (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport rejection → forcePose) that keeps hunger/stats/fall-damage server-authoritative, change-only per-player self-deltas, deadbanded 10 Hz mob replication with 5 s keyframes, chat with rate limits, backpressure shedding + slow-client kicks, join-restore/leave-persist through the v17 save, 60 s dirty persistence + SIGTERM drain, idle room eviction, /health + token-guarded /rooms diagnostics, PERSISTENCE=memory for DB-less runs, a netProbe CLI client, and Dockerfile + fly.toml. The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).
10	- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.
11	
12	### Changed
13

### Added

- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link — the offline single-player game is entirely unchanged and still needs no account or connection. The menu grows an **Online Worlds** section (create a server-backed world, copy an invite link) and an **Account** panel (one-click guest, or upgrade to keep your worlds); opening an invite link (`/join/<token>`) signs the visitor in — as a guest if they're new — accepts the membership, and drops the world into their list. In-world you see the other players (named avatars overhead), share every block edit / mob / chest / day-night with them, and **chat** with `T`/`Enter`; a ping badge and disconnect notice track the connection. The client mounts the **same** renderer/audio/HUD/input stack on a *replica* engine (`NetworkSession`, `lib/net/`): it worldgens byte-identically from the server's seed, applies the gzipped world sync, predicts only its own movement (streamed at tick rate; the server clamps speed/teleports and owns hunger/health/inventory via change-only self-deltas), renders remote players and mobs ~125 ms in the past from interpolation buffers, and reroutes gameplay commands up the wire through the engine's `routeDispatch` hook — so the input controller and every UI panel behave exactly as in single-player. Pause is personal (the world keeps running; "Save & Quit" becomes "Leave world"), the night skips only when everyone's in bed, and mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT). A full-stack Playwright spec (`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`) drives two browsers through invite → join → shared edit → chat against the real Next app (on an in-process `pglite://memory` Postgres) and Bun game server, no external services. **v1 scope cuts**: rafts/ships aren't boardable online, in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only their hits), and advancements/stats accrue to the room's primary player only.
- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + two HUD components; the
architecture of the replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

v1 scope cuts to know about (all documented where they bite): rafts/ships
can't be boarded online (a mounted pose is server-driven, which would fight
the client-owned pose stream); in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only
their hits); advancements/stats don't accrue in server rooms; indirect mob
kills credit the primary player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bunx drizzle-kit migrate      # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun server/index.ts           # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server, phase 4): shares `DATABASE_URL` and
  `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` with the web app.

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this).
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics (players, tick, slowest-tick ms);

Online multiplayer v1 (approved plan: `~/.claude/plans/implement-online-multiplayer-deployed-compressed-spindle.md`, 2026-07-03).

**Decisions (user-confirmed):** 2–8 player invite-link co-op, full-world rooms (no chunking/interest mgmt in v1); Vercel (Next app + better-auth + Neon Postgres + world/save/invite/ticket API) + Fly.io (Bun WebSocket game server, one `GameEngine` room per world @20Hz, Dockerfile portable to Railway); server-authoritative world with client-owned own-avatar movement (hybrid); better-auth anonymous plugin for guest→upgrade keeping worlds; SP stays fully offline/localStorage, same engine.

**Delivery (user decision 2026-07-03): ONE branch `feat/online-multiplayer`, all phases as commit slices on it, ONE PR at the end** (matches their "big work = one reviewable unit" rule; keep verify gate green at each phase boundary, lint green per commit). Phases: 1 deterministic foundations → 2 players-map engine core (save v17; existing e2e must pass unchanged) → 3 accounts/Postgres/cloud saves → 4 game server + protocol v1 → 5 client online play (NetworkSession + replica engine) → 6 hardening/ops → v0.13.0.

**Progress:** Phase 1 COMPLETE (first 4 commits on `feat/online-multiplayer`, unpushed, 2026-07-03): portable worldgen noise (`lib/world/noise.ts`, WORLDGEN_VERSION 10→11, digests in `lib/world/generationBaselines.ts`, Chromium≡Bun proven by `e2e/determinism.e2e.ts`); tick drivers (`lib/game/engine/tickDriver.ts` — accumulator + fixed 20Hz ticker for the server); FrameInput → abstract move intents (DOM codes/CapsLock/pointer lock now controller-only; `frameInput` test builder in `lib/game/engine/testSupport.ts`; e2e uses `forcePointerLock` hook). Full gate + 19/19 e2e green. Manual gameplay pass (terrain look, 4 world types) still pending — user's call before PR.

**Phase 2 IN PROGRESS** (commits 6566028..d9f6d73 on the branch, all unit tests + e2e green at each): players map + alias layer (installPlayerAliases in `lib/game/engine/players.ts`; aliases = shell/tests only, systems take PlayerState params); vitals/body/action systems converted to `(state, player, …)`; mobAI hunts nearest-targetable + anchors on nearest player (helpers `nearestPlayerTo`/`nearestTargetablePlayer` in players.ts); explosions/mob-arrows hit all/any players; per-player damage plumbing (`damageCombat`/`damageEnvironmental`/`triggerGameOver(player)` in GameEngine, single-arg wrappers still bound to primary); spawn directors per-wave center player + party cap scale + any-player spawner arming; randomTicks budget split; vehicles per-player; raid rewards all; weather keys primary. Loose test fixtures use self-referential flat states (`state.player = state`) or `GameState & PlayerState` intersection casts.

**Phase 2 COMPLETE** (branch now 13 commits, through 8babc93, 2026-07-03; full gate + 19/19 e2e green): everything above plus save v17 (`players: SavedPlayer[]`, `migrateSaveV16toV17`, owner/rider→PlayerId), dispatch/applyLook playerId attribution, per-player `stepPlayer` loop + `setPlayerInput`, `authority`("local"/"server")+`headless` engine options, `addPlayer`/`removePlayer` (serialize-on-leave/restore-on-join) + playerJoined/playerLeft events, all-players sleep gate + `wakeUp` command, ESLint alias guard for systems/, `GameEngine.multiplayer.test.ts` (9 tests), docs+CHANGELOG. **PR #43 OPEN (draft)** since 2026-07-03 — https://github.com/hutusi/monecraft/pull/43; branch pushed, CI runs per push.

**Phase 3 COMPLETE** (commits 10b769e/83908bc/903170a, pushed; full gate + 19/19 e2e): Drizzle schema (`db/schema.ts`, migrations committed, PGlite test fixture `db/testDb.ts`), better-auth 1.6.23 + anonymous plugin with onLinkAccount re-parenting (integration-tested FIRST on real SQL incl. duplicate-membership collision — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts`), worlds domain in `lib/online/worldsService.ts` (membership-gated CRUD/invites/LWW blobs/ticket mint, 9 tests) + thin app/api routes, `lib/net/tickets.ts` (HS256 60s, total verify), lazy `lib/auth/client.ts` + `minecraft_online_v1` offline-first gate, AccountPanel in ProfileSelect, `lib/game/cloudSaves.ts` gzip push/pull transport, .env.example + docker-compose, docs/online.md. DEFERRED to Phase 5 shell rework: cloud world-list merge + autosave sync wiring (transport ready), apiFor(playerId).

**Phase 4 COMPLETE** (commits 42047b0/f9fa943, NOT pushed — user said no push; full gate green, 1057 tests): protocol v1 (lib/net/protocol.ts catalog + total validators + command allow-list; codec gzip world-sync; clock EWMA), engine gains applyRemotePose (clamps + fall-damage/hunger synthesis via PlayerState.remoteMove) + bootPlayer:false (playerless rooms; headless snapshot stub; observeProgress guards missing primary) + worldTypeName getter, server/ (index Bun.serve /health /rooms /ws hello-deadline; room.ts fake-socket-testable Room with self-deltas/deadband/keyframes/backpressure/persist-merge; roomRegistry idle-evict; persistence drizzle+memory with readSave-shim parseSaveBlob; Dockerfile+fly.toml), scripts/netProbe.ts, docs/protocol.md + online.md ops. All Phase 5 implementation and documentation is complete. The monitor is watching the full e2e suite and will notify me when it finishes. Here's where things stand:

**Phase 5 — Client online play: complete, committed locally, not pushed** (per your standing instruction).

What I finished this session (the remaining Phase 5 deliverables — MP e2e, docs, CHANGELOG):

- **Daemon-free e2e stack**: extracted the schema into `db/ddl.ts`, added a `pglite://memory` runtime branch to `db()` (lazy-required, `serverExternalPackages` in `next.config.mjs`), and made `playwright.config.ts` a two-server array — the Next prod build on an in-process Postgres plus `bun server/index.ts` with `PERSISTENCE=memory`. No Docker, no cloud.
- **`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`**: two guest browser contexts — host creates an online world through the menus and mints an invite, friend joins via `/join/<token>`, both replicas see `players.size===2`, a host block break reaches both block journals, and chat round-trips.
- **Bug found and fixed by the e2e**: the replica boots `bootPlayer:false` but *not* headless, so the constructor's `buildSnapshot()` dereferenced the missing primary and threw `"Unknown player id: local"`. Fixed by stubbing the snapshot until the primary is seated and building the real one in `addPlayer` — with a regression test.
- **Docs**: manual "Playing online" section + `T`/`Enter` control; architecture's new "Multiplayer client (`lib/net/`)" section plus `replica`/`bootPlayer`/`routeDispatch`/`applyRemotePose` and `remotePlayerVisuals`; online.md client section + no-Docker dev; testing.md coverage rows + two-server note; README blurb; CHANGELOG "Online co-op multiplayer" entry. Added a `server` npm script.

**Gate so far green**: lint, typecheck, format:check, 1062 unit tests, build, and the multiplayer e2e in isolation. The full Playwright suite is running now to confirm the offline specs still pass under the two-server config — I'll report and then commit the final Phase 5 slice once it's green.

Note: **Phase 6** (reconnect ladder, latency sim, replay, kick, soak → v0.13.0) is still pending. You authorized "phase 4, 5" — I'll hold for your go-ahead before starting 6.

done

feat(net): reconnect ladder + simulated-latency knob

Harden the client session against dropped sockets. The replica engine now
outlives the WebSocket: a non-fatal close (idle timeout, server restart,
abnormal 1006) walks a back-off ladder (1/2/4/8/8 s, RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS),

minute after a drop — and redoing the handshake, which re-syncs the same
replica in place. Fatal closes (bad ticket, protocol mismatch, room full,
kicked, slow-client) don't retry; the disconnect modal shows only after the
ladder is exhausted. The roster reconciles on every world-sync so players
who left mid-outage are pruned, not left as ghosts.

runtime via window.__monecraft.net, or seeded from NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS)

and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Reconnect

The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
same room in place. The server closes the player's *previous* socket with
`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.

# Wire protocol (v1)

The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.

## Transport & framing

WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
contract, not the encoding.

## Handshake

1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).

A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.

## Steady state

**Client → server**

- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
  distance stats, and fall damage.
- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.

**Server → client**

- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
  sent only on change.
- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.

Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.

## Close codes

| Code | Meaning                                           |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          |
| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         |
| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      |
| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) |
| 4004 | idle timeout                                      |
| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) |
| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              |

## Trust model

The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
rewind validation would need.

`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this).
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics (players, tick, slowest-tick ms);
  requires `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.
- `PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the
  Playwright multiplayer spec, and `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (a CLI client
  that joins, walks, and tallies traffic — point it at localhost or staging).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

input.new_string:
All admin endpoints require `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN` (absent
`ADMIN_TOKEN` = always 403):

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this); unauthenticated.
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics: players, tick, `slowestTickMs`
  (against the 50 ms budget), and `kbOutPerSec` (downstream bandwidth). Watch
  these to set `MAX_ROOMS`.
- `GET /rooms/:id/log` — the room's rolling replay log (recent commands with
  their claimed eye pose + per-second pose anchors, `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE`
  entries). Feed a dump to `bun scripts/replay.ts dump.json` to reconstruct
  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

  the command-driven state offline (edits/inventory/movement — mobs aren't
  reproduced; the live RNG is unseeded).
- `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId` — eject a player (fatal `4003`, no retry).

`PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the Playwright
multiplayer spec, and the two CLI clients: `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (one
client, joins/walks/tallies) and `bun scripts/loadSim.ts <url> <world> <N>
<seconds>` (N synthetic clients → server tick p95 + bandwidth, for capacity
tuning). Both mint their own ticket, so `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` must match; give
`loadSim` `ADMIN_TOKEN` too for the server-side stats.

### Runbook

- **A player is stuck / griefing.** The world owner revokes shared invite
  links from the menu ("Revoke links" on the world card — kills every
  outstanding link at once; existing members keep access). To force a live
  player out, `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`.
- **A redeploy.** SIGTERM drains every room (persist + close with `4005`);
  clients reconnect on the ladder to the new instance and re-sync. Loss is
  bounded to the last 60 s (the dirty-persist interval) even on a hard crash.
- **"How did this happen?"** Pull `/rooms/:id/log`, then `bun scripts/replay.ts`
  to replay the command stream against a fresh engine and diff the outcome.
- **Latency feels bad.** From a browser console, `window.__monecraft.net`
  `.setSimulatedLatency(ms)` injects delay to reproduce; set
  `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` to bake it into a dev build.
- **Capacity.** Run `loadSim` at the target player count and watch
  `slowestTickMs`/`kbOutPerSec` in `/rooms`; keep p95 well under 50 ms and set
  `MAX_ROOMS` so peak memory (~74 MB/room) fits the machine. Net constants
  (deadbands, keyframe/persist intervals, reconnect ladder) live in
  [tuning.md](tuning.md#multiplayer-networking).

# Online: accounts, cloud saves, multiplayer

How the online stack fits together, and how to run it. The offline
single-player game needs **none** of this: without an online action, the
client never makes an auth request (the `minecraft_online_v1` localStorage
flag gates even the session check).

## The pieces

```
Browser ──(cookies)── Next.js app          ── Neon/Postgres
   │                   /api/auth/*   better-auth (guests + accounts)
   │                   /api/worlds…  world CRUD, invites, cloud saves
   │                   /api/worlds/:id/ticket   mints 60s HS256 join ticket
   │
   └──(ws + ticket)── Game server (Bun, Fly.io)  ── same Postgres
                       one authoritative GameEngine room per world (phase 4)
```

The web app and the game server never talk to each other at runtime: the
join ticket (`lib/net/tickets.ts`, signed with the shared
`GAME_TICKET_SECRET`) is the only trust link, and both read the same
Postgres.

## Identity: guests first

- "Play online as guest" (menu → Account panel) creates a real better-auth
  user with `isAnonymous` — no form, instant play. Guests own worlds and
  memberships like anyone else.
- Upgrading (sign-up, or sign-in to an existing account, while holding the
  guest session) triggers the anonymous plugin's `onLinkAccount` hook
  (`lib/auth/server.ts`): worlds, memberships, and invites re-parent onto the
  new account before the guest row is deleted. **This hook is the "guests
  keep their worlds" promise** — `lib/auth/auth.test.ts` proves it against
  the real better-auth flow on real SQL (PGlite), including the
  duplicate-membership collision case.
- Sessions are better-auth cookies; the game server never sees them.

## Worlds, invites, cloud saves

`lib/online/worldsService.ts` owns the rules (membership-gated reads that
present as `not-found` so ids can't be probed; owner-gated rename/delete/
invite; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses). The `app/api`
routes are thin HTTP adapters over it.

Single-player cloud saves are gzipped `SaveData` blobs (`lib/game/
cloudSaves.ts` — block diffs compress extremely well) with last-write-wins
concurrency: each device sends the `updatedAt` stamp it last saw
(`x-base-updated-at`); a mismatch is **409** and the client pulls the newer
save before retrying. The transport is built and tested; surfacing it in the
world list / autosave UX is still to come.

## Playing online (client)

The menu's **Online Worlds** section (`WorldSelect`) lists every world the
signed-in user may play, creates new ones (same form as local worlds — the
row lives in Postgres, the game server hosts it), and mints invite links
(`/join/<token>` — the landing page resolves the token, signs the visitor in
as a guest if needed, and accepts the membership). Playing one runs
`GameShell.playOnline`: ensure a session → `POST /api/worlds/:id/ticket` →
`connectNetworkSession(gameServerUrl, ticket)` → mount the game on the
session's replica engine. The connection lifecycle (chat, ping badge,
disconnect modal, leave) lives in the session + two HUD components; the
architecture of the replica/routing/interpolation stack is in
[architecture.md](architecture.md#multiplayer-client-libnet).

v1 scope cuts to know about (all documented where they bite): rafts/ships
can't be boarded online (a mounted pose is server-driven, which would fight
the client-owned pose stream); in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only
their hits); advancements/stats don't accrue in server rooms; indirect mob
kills credit the primary player.

## Environment & local development

See `.env.example` for every variable (web: `DATABASE_URL`,
`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `GAME_TICKET_SECRET`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_GAME_SERVER_URL`; game server adds `PORT`, `PERSISTENCE`,
`ADMIN_TOKEN`).

```bash
docker compose up -d          # local Postgres (dev only — tests use PGlite)
bunx drizzle-kit migrate      # apply db/migrations once
bun run dev                   # web app with accounts + API
bun run server                # game server (ws://localhost:8080)
```

Full co-op on localhost: run all three, open two browser windows (one
normal, one private — separate guest identities), create an online world in
the first, and paste its invite link into the second.

**No Docker at all**: `DATABASE_URL=pglite://memory` runs the web app on an
ephemeral in-process Postgres (`db/index.ts` applies the schema from
`db/ddl.ts` at boot; data lives as long as the process). Pair it with the
game server's `PERSISTENCE=memory` and the whole online stack is two
commands with zero services — exactly how the Playwright multiplayer suite
boots it (`playwright.config.ts`).

Schema lives in `db/schema.ts` (drizzle); migrations are generated with
`bunx drizzle-kit generate` and committed under `db/migrations/`. The PGlite
fixture (`db/testDb.ts`) applies the same DDL in-memory so `bun test` needs
no daemon; the auth integration test exercises every table, which keeps the
fixture DDL and the schema module honest against each other.

## Production

- **Vercel**: set the web env vars; point `DATABASE_URL` at Neon. The auth
  mount builds lazily, so `next build` needs no env.
- **Fly.io** (game server, phase 4): shares `DATABASE_URL` and
  `GAME_TICKET_SECRET` with the web app.

## Game server operations

`server/index.ts` (Bun, no build step — `bun server/index.ts`). One process
hosts up to `MAX_ROOMS` worlds; each room is an authoritative `GameEngine`
on the drift-corrected 20 Hz ticker. Rooms load from Postgres on first join,
persist every 60 s (when dirty), on last-leave, and on SIGTERM (deploys
drain, ≤60 s loss crash-safe); five idle minutes evicts a room from memory.
See [protocol.md](protocol.md) for the wire format.

- `GET /health` — liveness (Fly checks hit this).
- `GET /rooms` — per-room diagnostics (players, tick, slowest-tick ms);
  requires `Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN`.
- `PERSISTENCE=memory` runs with no database — local iteration, the
  Playwright multiplayer spec, and `bun scripts/netProbe.ts` (a CLI client
  that joins, walks, and tallies traffic — point it at localhost or staging).

Deploy: `server/Dockerfile` + `server/fly.toml` (see file comments). The
container is platform-neutral — anything that runs a long-lived container
with WebSocket ingress works.

## Inventory

`HOTBAR_SLOTS`, `INVENTORY_SLOTS`, `MAX_STACK_SIZE`. **Save-sensitive** — see below.

`CHEST_SLOTS` (27) is the storage capacity of a placed chest, read by the interact,
mining, and save paths (`lib/game/engine/systems/interact.ts`, `…/mining.ts`,
`lib/game/save.ts`) and the inventory panel grid. It is **soft** save-sensitive:
shrinking it after chests have been saved with items past the new limit would drop
those overflow slots on load (`readContainers` rebuilds a `CHEST_SLOTS`-length array).

## Persistence & rendering

`AUTOSAVE_INTERVAL_MS`, `WORLDGEN_VERSION`, `SAVE_KEY` (legacy), `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS`,
`RENDER_RADIUS`, `RENDER_GRID`, `THIRD_PERSON_DISTANCE`, `THIRD_PERSON_MARGIN`.

`RENDER_RADIUS` is the biggest **performance** lever: the renderer meshes one region
of this radius around the player, so larger values draw more terrain at higher cost;
`RENDER_GRID` is how far the player moves before that mesh rebuilds (smaller = more
frequent rebuilds, fresher view). `STUCK_RESET_SECONDS` is how long an overlap is
tolerated before the auto-unstuck teleport fires.

## Save- and worldgen-sensitive tunables

Change these only with care:

- **`WORLDGEN_VERSION`** (`10`) is the worldgen baseline each world records at
  creation. When a deliberate terrain change invalidates old block-diffs, bump this:
  every world whose recorded version differs discards its stale diffs and reboots from
  its seed — per-world, without renaming any key (see [save-format.md](save-format.md)).
  This replaced the old whole-store `SAVE_KEY` bump, which reset _every_ world at once.
  It's versioned independently of the save **schema** (currently v16); don't bump it to
  express a schema change — add a migration instead.
- **`SAVE_KEY`** (`"minecraft_save_v7"`) is now **legacy**: each world has its own
  `minecraft_world_save_<id>` key, and `SAVE_KEY` is read only once by the one-time
  migration. Leave it alone.
- **`INVENTORY_SLOTS` / `HOTBAR_SLOTS` / `MAX_STACK_SIZE`** affect the saved
  inventory layout. `save.ts` already migrates the v1 (40-slot) → v2 (36-slot)
  change; altering these again needs a matching migration or old saves break.
- **Daylight thresholds and `WAKE_DAY_PHASE`** shape the persisted `dayClock`'s
  meaning but are not save-format-breaking on their own.

## Multiplayer networking

Server-side constants live in `server/room.ts` and `lib/net/protocol.ts` (not
`config.ts` — they shape the wire and the room budget, not gameplay balance).
None affect single-player, and none are save-sensitive.

- **`ROOM_CAPACITY`** (`8`, protocol.ts) — max players per world. The v1 co-op
  scale the whole design assumes; raising it grows the per-tick pose/self fan-out
  quadratically, so re-measure with `loadSim` before nudging it.
- **`MAX_ROOMS`** (env, default `6`) — worlds one process hosts (memory: ~74 MB
  each). Joins beyond it are refused at the door, not thrashed. Tune from
  `/rooms` p95 tick + peak memory.
- **Tick rate** — `TICK_SECONDS` (`0.05` = 20 Hz, `tickDriver.ts`) is the room
  sim + pose-stream cadence. The whole latency budget hangs off it; not a
  casual dial.
- **Replication cadence** — `KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`100` = 5 s, full mob
  keyframe / drift correction), mob delta frames at **10 Hz** (half tick rate)
  with `MOB_DEADBAND_SQ` (`0.05²` — smaller = more mob updates, more bandwidth),
  `DAY_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`20` = 1 s day-clock sync), `POSE_CHECKPOINT_TICKS`
  (`20` = 1 s replay-log pose anchors). `INTERPOLATION_DELAY_MS` (`125`,
  `lib/net/interpolation.ts`) is how far in the past remote entities render —
  larger absorbs more jitter at the cost of visible lag.
- **Backpressure** — `BACKPRESSURE_SOFT_BYTES` (256 KB → shed `pp`/`mp`),
  `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_BYTES` (1 MB) + `BACKPRESSURE_KICK_STRIKES` (~5 s sustained
  → `4008` kick).
- **Persistence** — `PERSIST_INTERVAL_TICKS` (`1200` = 60 s dirty-persist; also
  the crash-loss bound), idle-evict at 5 min (`roomRegistry.ts`).
- **Reconnect** — `RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` (`[1,2,4,8,8] s`, protocol.ts) is the
  client back-off ladder; the join ticket TTL is `TICKET_TTL_SECONDS` (`60`,
  `tickets.ts`).
- **Replay log** — `COMMAND_LOG_SIZE` (env, default `4096`) bounds each room's
  in-memory command ring dumped by `/rooms/:id/log`.
- **Latency sim** — `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS` (env, default `0`) seeds
  the client's artificial one-way delay; `window.__monecraft.net.setSimulatedLatency(ms)`
  overrides it live.

content.text: Now the CHANGELOG Phase 6 entries and the architecture.md multiplayer-client note. Let me add the CHANGELOG entry:

input.old_string:
### Added

- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link
input.new_string:
### Added

- **Multiplayer hardening & ops**: the online session now survives dropped connections and ships an operator toolkit. The replica engine outlives its socket — a non-fatal drop (idle timeout, redeploy, network blip) walks a back-off ladder (1/2/4/8/8 s), mints a **fresh** join ticket each rung, and re-handshakes to re-sync the same world in place (an amber "Reconnecting…" badge, not a dead-end modal); fatal closes (bad ticket, kick, slow-client) don't retry. A `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` knob on `window.__monecraft.net` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`) injects artificial delay for local testing. World owners can **revoke every outstanding invite link** in one click from the menu. The game server gains admin ops behind `ADMIN_TOKEN`: a per-room replay log (`GET /rooms/:id/log`) that `scripts/replay.ts` reconstructs offline, an owner **kick** (`POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`), and `/rooms` bandwidth (`kbOutPerSec`) alongside the tick gauges — plus `scripts/loadSim.ts`, a synthetic N-client soak that reports server tick p95 vs the 50 ms budget for tuning `MAX_ROOMS`. Net constants are documented in tuning.md and an ops runbook in online.md.
- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link

lines: +- **Multiplayer hardening & ops**: the online session now survives dropped connections and ships an operator toolkit. The replica engine outlives its socket — a non-fatal drop (idle timeout, redeploy, network blip) walks a back-off ladder (1/2/4/8/8 s), mints a **fresh** join ticket each rung, and re-handshakes to re-sync the same world in place (an amber "Reconnecting…" badge, not a dead-end modal); fatal closes (bad ticket, kick, slow-client) don't retry. A `setSimulatedLatency(ms)` knob on `window.__monecraft.net` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_NET_SIM_LATENCY_MS`) injects artificial delay for local testing. World owners can **revoke every outstanding invite link** in one click from the menu. The game server gains admin ops behind `ADMIN_TOKEN`: a per-room replay log (`GET /rooms/:id/log`) that `scripts/replay.ts` reconstructs offline, an owner **kick** (`POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`), and `/rooms` bandwidth (`kbOutPerSec`) alongside the tick gauges — plus `scripts/loadSim.ts`, a synthetic N-client soak that reports server tick p95 vs the 50 ms budget for tuning `MAX_ROOMS`. Net constants are documented in tuning.md and an ops runbook in online.md.

- **Online co-op multiplayer**: 2–8 players in one shared, server-hosted world via a private invite link — the offline single-player game is entirely unchanged and still needs no account or connection. The menu grows an **Online Worlds** section (create a server-backed world, copy an invite link) and an **Account** panel (one-click guest, or upgrade to keep your worlds); opening an invite link (`/join/<token>`) signs the visitor in — as a guest if they're new — accepts the membership, and drops the world into their list. In-world you see the other players (named avatars overhead), share every block edit / mob / chest / day-night with them, and **chat** with `T`/`Enter`; a ping badge and disconnect notice track the connection. The client mounts the **same** renderer/audio/HUD/input stack on a _replica_ engine (`NetworkSession`, `lib/net/`): it worldgens byte-identically from the server's seed, applies the gzipped world sync, predicts only its own movement (streamed at tick rate; the server clamps speed/teleports and owns hunger/health/inventory via change-only self-deltas), renders remote players and mobs ~125 ms in the past from interpolation buffers, and reroutes gameplay commands up the wire through the engine's `routeDispatch` hook — so the input controller and every UI panel behave exactly as in single-player. Pause is personal (the world keeps running; "Save & Quit" becomes "Leave world"), the night skips only when everyone's in bed, and mining is server-confirmed (~1 RTT). A full-stack Playwright spec (`e2e/multiplayer.e2e.ts`) drives two browsers through invite → join → shared edit → chat against the real Next app (on an in-process `pglite://memory` Postgres) and Bun game server, no external services. **v1 scope cuts**: rafts/ships aren't boardable online, in-flight arrows aren't replicated (only their hits), and advancements/stats accrue to the room's primary player only.

- **Multiplayer game server (groundwork)**: a Bun process hosting authoritative world rooms over WebSocket — protocol v1 (JSON envelopes + one gzipped world-sync frame; total validation of hostile input with a per-command allow-list), 20 Hz fixed-tick rooms with client-pose clamping (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport rejection → forcePose) that keeps hunger/stats/fall-damage server-authoritative, change-only per-player self-deltas, deadbanded 10 Hz mob replication with 5 s keyframes, chat with rate limits, backpressure shedding + slow-client kicks, join-restore/leave-persist through the v17 save, 60 s dirty persistence + SIGTERM drain, idle room eviction, /health + token-guarded /rooms diagnostics, PERSISTENCE=memory for DB-less runs, a netProbe CLI client, and Dockerfile + fly.toml. The engine gains authority-aware remote-pose application and can construct playerless rooms (bootPlayer: false).

- **Online accounts, cloud saves & invites (groundwork)**: better-auth identities with instant anonymous guests — upgrading to a real account (sign-up or sign-in while playing as guest) re-parents the guest's worlds/memberships/invites onto the new account, proven by an integration test against real better-auth + real SQL (PGlite). Drizzle/Postgres schema for worlds, memberships, and invite links; membership-gated world CRUD; idempotent invite acceptance with expiry/max-uses; gzipped single-player cloud-save blobs with last-write-wins conflict detection; and 60-second HS256 join tickets — the only trust link the future game server needs (it never sees cookies). Menu gains an Account panel. Fully offline-first: until the player takes an online action, the client makes no auth requests at all.

1	# Wire protocol (v1)
2	
3	The client↔game-server protocol, defined in `lib/net/protocol.ts` (single
4	source of truth — this page is the narrative). Versioned as a whole via
5	`PROTOCOL_VERSION`; join tickets stamp it, and a mismatch is refused at the
6	door, so format drift mid-session cannot happen.
7	
8	## Transport & framing
9	
10	WebSocket to the game server's `/ws`. Everything is a JSON text frame
11	discriminated on `t`, except **one binary frame**: the world sync (join and
12	`resync`), which is gzipped JSON — a fresh world's block diff is bytes, a
13	terraformed one compresses >2×. Hot paths (pose/tick) can move to packed
14	binary later without renegotiating anything: the envelope shape is the
15	contract, not the encoding.
16	
17	## Handshake
18	
19	1. Client connects and must send `hello { ticket, protocol }` within **5s**.
20	2. The server verifies the ticket (HS256, 60s TTL, minted by the web API —
21	   see [online.md](online.md)), checks `protocol === PROTOCOL_VERSION`, loads
22	   the room, and answers `welcome` + the binary `worldSync`.
23	3. Anything else → close with an application code (below).
24	
25	A client regenerates the world from `welcome.seed` (bit-identical since
26	worldgen v11 — see [testing.md](testing.md)) and applies `worldSync.changes`;
27	the join payload is KBs, not the 37 MB voxel field.
28	
29	## Steady state
30	
31	**Client → server**
32	
33	- `pose` @20 Hz — client-authoritative avatar movement + live intents.
34	  Clamped server-side (sprint-ceiling speed, jump/fall vertical, teleport
35	  rejection → `forcePose`); accepted movement drives server-side hunger,
36	  distance stats, and fall damage.
37	- `cmd` — a discrete `Command` + the claimed eye pose (applied through the
38	  same clamps before dispatch, so aimed raycasts resolve where the client
39	  looked). Validated against a per-type **allow-list**; local-presentation
40	  commands (pause/debug/camera) never travel. Budget: 60/s.
41	- `chat` (≤256 chars, 3/s), `ping`, `resync`.
42	
43	**Server → client**
44	
45	- `tick { n, ev, pp, mp, day?, self? }` @20 Hz — world events since last
46	  tick (block edits ride these), other players' poses, deadbanded mob poses
47	  (~10 Hz), the day clock every second, and `self`: the private, server-
48	  authoritative delta of YOUR state (inventory/hearts/hunger/xp/effects/…),
49	  sent only on change.
50	- `mobsKeyframe` every 5s (drift correction), `playerJoined`/`playerLeft`,
51	  `container` (open-chest updates), `chat`, `pong`, `forcePose`.
52	
53	Backpressure: past 256 KB buffered, a client's `pp`/`mp` are shed (events
54	and `self` still flow); sustained >1 MB is a `4008` kick.
55	
56	## Reconnect
57	
58	The replica engine outlives the socket. On a **non-fatal** drop the client
59	walks a back-off ladder (`RECONNECT_DELAYS_MS` = 1/2/4/8/8 s), minting a
60	**fresh** ticket each rung (the 60 s TTL kills a stale one) and doing a whole
61	new `hello` → `welcome` → world-sync — a reconnect is an ordinary join on a
62	new socket, not a special frame, so the server's `join` already re-syncs the
63	same room in place. The server closes the player's _previous_ socket with
64	`4003` when the new one lands (see the table). `resync` stays the same-socket
65	path (a client that's still connected but suspects drift asks for a fresh
66	world-sync + keyframe). Fatal closes are not retried; after the ladder is
67	exhausted the client shows the disconnect modal.
68	
69	## Close codes
70	
71	| Code | Meaning                                           | Client retries? |
72	| ---- | ------------------------------------------------- | --------------- |
73	| 4000 | bad/expired ticket (or no hello in time)          | no (fatal)      |
74	| 4001 | protocol version mismatch                         | no (fatal)      |
75	| 4002 | room full (8 players) or server at MAX_ROOMS      | no (fatal)      |
76	| 4003 | kicked (owner action, or replaced by a reconnect) | no (fatal)      |
77	| 4004 | idle timeout                                      | yes (ladder)    |
78	| 4005 | server shutting down (redeploy — reconnect after) | yes (ladder)    |
79	| 4008 | slow client (sustained backpressure)              | no (fatal)      |
80	| 1006 | abnormal close (network drop)                     | yes (ladder)    |
81	
82	## Trust model
83	
84	The server is authoritative for the world: every gameplay command executes
85	in ITS engine; clients cannot invent items or edits. The one client-owned
86	thing is each avatar's own movement (clamped, never trusted blindly). The
87	claimed eye pose on `cmd` is the hybrid model's soft spot — acceptable for
88	invite-only co-op, and the envelope already carries what stricter server-side
89	rewind validation would need.

1	# Testing
2	
3	Two runners, three layers:
4	
5	- **`bun test`** — unit, integration, and component tests, colocated as `*.test.ts[x]` next to the code they cover. The shared setup (`tests/setup.ts`, preloaded via `bunfig.toml`) registers happy-dom so React component tests run under the same runner; the game engine itself needs no DOM (see [architecture.md](architecture.md)).
6	- **`bun run test:e2e`** — Playwright browser smoke tests in `e2e/*.e2e.ts` against the production build. The file suffix matters: `bun test` auto-collects `*.test.ts` AND `*.spec.ts`, so E2E files must use `.e2e.ts`.
7	
8	## What is covered
9	
10	| Area                          | File                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | What it pins down                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
11	| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
12	| Worldgen determinism          | `lib/world/generation.test.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | SHA-256 digests of generated worlds per seed (the save-compat contract), plus structural probes, meshing snapshots, opaque/glass layer boundaries, thin door geometry, and dungeon presence — chests/spawners/mossy generate underground and `collectDungeonSites` reproduces every chest/spawner; plus per-world-type SHA-256 baselines (flat/amplified/islands) and shape probes (flat is level, amplified higher-relief, islands floods more with dry spawn land); **village** presence (houses build at each `collectVillageSites` center, the derive is deterministic, every center is clear of spawn) survives the re-baseline; **ocean flora** (kelp stands on sand under water, never breaches the surface-clearance band; coral sits on the floor), **shipwrecks** (fully submerged, a chest at every `collectShipwreckSites` index, derive deterministic), and **buried treasure** (a sand-capped chest in the beach band at every `collectTreasureSites` site, derive deterministic) — every generated chest belongs to a known dungeon/shipwreck/buried site                                                                                                                                                        |

input.content:
---
name: bun-test-exit-code
description: "Never gate on `bun test | tail` — piping hides Bun's exit code (99 = passed-but-leaked)"
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When verifying the monecraft suite, capture `bun test`'s **exit code**, don't just eyeball `| tail`. Bun exits **99** when every test passes but the run leaked an unhandled rejection (e.g. an unclosed PGlite/WASM handle) — and CI's `verify` job gates on the exit code, so it goes red while a piped local run looks green.

**Why:** In this repo, PR #43's `verify` was red for exactly this while `e2e`/CodeRabbit passed; the cause was PGlite test fixtures never `.close()`d (see [[multiplayer-project]] commit ad6f55e). A `bun test | tail -6` shows "0 fail" and the pipe's exit code is `tail`'s (0), so the 99 was invisible for several phases.

**How to apply:** Run `bun test > log 2>&1; echo "EXIT $?"` (or without a pipe) and require exit 0 — not just "0 fail". Any PGlite fixture (`createTestDb`) must be closed in `afterEach`/`afterAll` via `closeTestDb(db)`.

content.text:
Pushed and monitoring CI. Here's the full status.

## Phase 6 — Hardening + ops: complete, pushed ✅

**Pushed** `d030caa..ad6f55e` (6 commits) to `feat/online-multiplayer`. PR #43 now has the whole online-multiplayer feature (Phases 1–6). A fresh CI run (`verify` + `e2e` + CodeRabbit) is in progress — I'm monitoring it and will report when it lands.

**What shipped in Phase 6:**
- **Reconnect ladder** (`07df3a8`) — the replica engine outlives its socket; a non-fatal drop mints a fresh ticket and re-handshakes over a back-off ladder (1/2/4/8/8s), resuming the same world in place ("Reconnecting…" badge, not a dead modal). Plus a `setSimulatedLatency` knob on `window.__monecraft.net`, and a fake-socket `NetworkSession.test.ts` driving the whole lifecycle incl. drop→resume.
- **Server ops** (`1595d66`) — per-room replay log + `GET /rooms/:id/log` + `scripts/replay.ts` offline reconstruction, owner `kick` + `POST /rooms/:id/kick/:playerId`, `/rooms` bandwidth gauge.
- **Invite revocation** (`36d3b45`) — owner "Revoke links" button + service/API/tests.
- **loadSim** (`98d7ee5`) — synthetic N-client soak reporting server tick p95 vs the 50ms budget.
- **Docs** (`599ad28`) — protocol reconnect/close-codes, online.md ops runbook, tuning.md net constants, CHANGELOG.

**Critical find — the CI red was real** (`ad6f55e`): `bun test` was exiting **99** (1074 pass / 0 fail, but an unhandled rejection at exit) because the Phase 3 PGlite fixtures were never `.close()`d. It was invisible locally because I'd been piping `bun test | tail`, which drops the exit code — that's why PR #43's `verify` job was red while `e2e`/CodeRabbit passed. Fixed with `closeTestDb` + `afterEach`/`afterAll`. **Full suite now exits 0**, and I saved a memory so I never gate on a piped `bun test` again.

**Local gate green** (with real exit codes checked): lint, typecheck, format:check, `bun test` (1074, exit 0), build, e2e (20/20).

## One thing needing your call

CodeRabbit left **24 inline comments** on the pushed code (1 Critical at `server/room.ts:242`, several Major). You interrupted before I could read them. ID: 3519440947
---

**Fire-and-forget `client.exec(SCHEMA_DDL)` has no error handling.**
If schema initialization fails, the rejection is unobserved (unhandled promise rejection) instead of surfacing a clear startup error, since the promise is discarded with `void` and never awaited or caught.
=====================
FILE: lib/game/engine/GameEngine.ts:457
ID: 3519440964
---
_🔒 Security & Privacy_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Cap `elapsedSeconds` inside `applyRemotePose` as defense-in-depth against the unbounded-clamp exploit.**
This is the shared validation entry point for both `"pose"` and `"cmd"` messages in `server/room.ts`. As described in the companion critical comment on `server/room.ts`, `elapsed` can currently grow without bound when a client withholds/loses pose acceptance, which linearly inflates `maxHorizontal`/`maxUp`/`maxDown` and eventually admits an arbitrary jump. Capping `elapsed` here protects the invariant regardless of caller bugs.
=====================
FILE: lib/net/NetworkSession.ts:470
ID: 3519440975
---
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Keep the cmd pose out of the authoritative position.** `applyRemotePose` writes the supplied `y` back into `player.position`, so the eye-height `cmd` pose can briefly move the broadcast/self-delta position up by 1.62 until the next pose tick. Reuse `EYE_HEIGHT` instead of hardcoding `1.62`.

ID: 3519440986

**Add an `EnchantmentId` allow-list for `enchant`.** `setGameMode`, `setDifficulty`, and `creativeGiveItem` are already rejected downstream, but `enchant` still passes an arbitrary string into `canEnchant`, which indexes `ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[id]` and can throw on a bad id.
=====================

ID: 3519440992
---
_🔒 Security & Privacy_ | _🟡 Minor_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Gate `cmd` by owner role**  
`ClientConn.role` is never checked on the `cmd` path, so any member can reach `engine.dispatch(...)` and change room-wide settings like `setDifficulty`. If those controls are owner-only, block non-owners before dispatch.
=====================
FILE: server/room.ts:202
ID: 3519441000
---
_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Reconnecting players can be wrongly rejected as "room full".**
The capacity check (`this.clients.size >= ROOM_CAPACITY`) runs *before* the stale-connection lookup/replacement for the same `claims.sub`. When the room is already at capacity, an already-connected member trying to reconnect (e.g. after a dropped socket) is counted against their own slot and gets kicked with `CLOSE_ROOM_FULL` instead of being allowed to replace their stale connection.
=====================
FILE: server/room.ts:304
ID: 3519441015
---
_🔒 Security & Privacy_ | _🔴 Critical_ | _⚡ Quick win_
**Advance `lastPoseTick` on accepted `cmd` poses in `server/room.ts:234-239`**  
`lastPoseTick` only advances in the `"pose"` path, so skipping pose updates or replaying rejected ones lets `elapsed` grow without bound. Since `applyRemotePose()` scales its clamp linearly with `elapsed`, a client can eventually make arbitrarily large `cmd`-driven jumps. The `this.rooms.size >= this.maxRooms` check (Line 34) doesn't account for rooms currently loading in `this.loading`. content.text:
I've now read and verified all 25. First, the good news: **CI is fully green** (verify ✅ e2e ✅ CodeRabbit ✅) — the PGlite fix cleared the red `verify`.

Here's my triage of the 25 CodeRabbit findings, verified against the actual code:

## A. Real bugs — should fix (no design call needed)

**Security / server (highest priority):**
- **🔴 Critical `server/room.ts` — unbounded pose clamp** (+ its Major companion in `GameEngine.ts:457`): the `cmd` path computes `elapsed` from `lastPoseTick` but never *advances* it, and `applyRemotePose` scales its speed clamp linearly with `elapsed` — so a client that sends only `cmd`s can eventually teleport. Real speed-hack vector. Fix: advance `lastPoseTick` on accepted cmd poses **and** cap `elapsed`.
- **`server/room.ts:202` (Major)** — a member reconnecting to a *full* room is rejected `ROOM_FULL` because the capacity check counts their own stale slot before the replacement runs. Fix: skip the capacity check when `claims.sub` is already connected.
- **`server/roomRegistry.ts:34` (Major)** — `MAX_ROOMS` TOCTOU: concurrent loads of different worlds ignore the in-flight `loading` map. Fix: count `rooms.size + loading.size`.
- **`lib/net/protocol.ts:229` (Major)** — `enchant` passes an arbitrary string into `canEnchant`/`ENCHANTMENT_DEFS[id]`; add an id allow-list like the other commands.

**Engine correctness (some affect single-player too):**
- **`GameEngine.ts:721` (Major)** — `applyMoveStack` uses `state.inventory`/`openContainerIndex` (primary aliases), so a non-primary player's chest/inventory move hits the *primary's* inventory. Real MP data bug.
- **`GameEngine.ts:1019` (Major)** — `restorePlayerFields` never reads the persisted `gameMode`/`gameOver` it serializes; a rejoining player loses their mode.
- **`players.ts:128` (Major)** — `nearestTargetablePlayer` doesn't skip dead players, so mobs target corpses (SP too). One-liner.
- **`playerStats.ts:86` (Major)** — hardcore game-over hearts get topped back to `MAX_HEARTS` next tick, overwriting the `hearts=0` withered state (SP hardcore too). One-liner guard.

**Web-app concurrency:**
- **`worldsService.ts:171` (Major)** — cloud-save LWW check-then-act races; fold the stale compare into the `UPDATE` predicate + check affected rows.
- **`worldsService.ts:226` (Major)** — invite `maxUses` check-then-act races; enforce the cap at write time.
- **`auth/server.ts:62` (Major)** — the guest→account re-parenting does 4 non-atomic writes then deletes the guest; wrap in `db.transaction` (the "guests keep worlds" promise).

**Client robustness / my Phase 5–6 code:**
- **`db/index.ts:36` (Minor)** — `void client.exec(SCHEMA_DDL)` swallows a DDL failure as an unhandled rejection; `.catch` it.
- **`GameShell.tsx:105` (Major)** — `playOnline` isn't re-entrancy-guarded; a double-click leaks a WebSocket. Guard on `connecting`.
- **`room.ts:121` (Minor)** — my `kbOutPerSec` is a *lifetime* average, not "since last read" as the comment claims; window it.
- **`AccountPanel.tsx:48` (Minor)** — no try/catch around the auth awaits; a network reject strands the button `disabled`.
- **`NetworkSession.ts:470` (Minor)** — the `cmd` eye-pose (`y+1.62`) gets written into the authoritative foot position for a tick.
- **`WorldSelect.tsx:87` (Minor)** — a failed `createOnlineWorld` closes the form silently, no error shown.
- **`GameEngine.ts:1044` (Major)** — if the last awake player leaves, sleeping players aren't re-checked and can hang. Small.

## B. Real, but a design call is yours
- **`server/room.ts:77` (Minor)** — any member can send `setDifficulty`/`setGameMode`. Should these be **owner-only** in co-op? (I'd say yes.)
- **`GameShell.tsx:164` (Minor)** — online Game Over "delete" only returns to the menu; it doesn't delete the world server-side. Wire it to `DELETE /api/worlds/:id`, or hide the button? (v1 scope.)

## C. Not real / already handled — skip
- **`save/route.ts:37`** — NaN `x-save-version` is already rejected by `putSaveBlob`'s `Number.isInteger` guard → 400. (Defense-in-depth only.)
- **`GameEngine.ts:1157`** — CodeRabbit self-marked "✅ Addressed"; it's the documented v1 scope cut (server rooms track no advancements/stats).
- **`save.ts:275` (inventoryCounts)** — verified: a v16 save can't carry the pre-v2 `inventoryCounts` format, so the migration never loses it in practice. Harmless 1-line hardening at most.
- **`save/route.ts:40`** (pre-buffer size check) — minor DoS hardening on an auth-gated route; low value.

---

That's ~18 genuine fixes. Most are small; the concurrency ones (transactions, atomic updates) and the pose-clamp Critical are the substantive ones.

fix(server): address review — pose-clamp, capacity, and command hardening

From CodeRabbit's review of the multiplayer PR:

- **Critical speed-hack**: the `cmd` path never advanced `lastPoseTick`, so a
  client sending only commands let `elapsed` grow unbounded and inflate
  applyRemotePose's linear speed clamp until any jump passed. Advance the
  pose clock on an accepted cmd pose too (the elapsed cap in GameEngine is the
  companion defense).
- **Reconnect wrongly rejected as room-full**: the capacity check counted a
  member's own stale slot; skip it when the id is already connected, so a
  dropped socket can always return.
- **World settings gated to the owner**: `setDifficulty`/`setGameMode` change
  the world for everyone — reject them from non-owner members before dispatch.
- **enchant allow-list**: an unknown enchant id reached `canEnchant` and threw
  (indexing ENCHANTMENT_DEFS); validate it in readCommand with hasOwnProperty
  (not `in`, so `__proto__`/`toString` can't slip through).
- **cmd pose is the foot, not the eye**: the client sent eye height (y+1.62),
  which the server wrote into the authoritative foot position and the engine
  then re-offset by EYE_HEIGHT — send the foot pose like the stream does.
- **MAX_ROOMS TOCTOU**: count in-flight loads so two concurrent loads of
  different worlds can't both slip past the cap.
- **Bandwidth gauge windowed**: `kbOutPerSec` was a lifetime average; report
  the delta since the last diagnostics read.

Tests: owner-only settings, reconnect into a full room, a cmd-only client's
jump still clamped, the enchant allow-list, and the windowed gauge.
EOF

Engine correctness findings from the multiplayer PR review, several of which
also affect single-player:

- **moveStack hit the primary alias**: `applyMoveStack` used
  `state.inventory`/`state.openContainerIndex` (primary-player aliases), so a
  non-primary player moving stacks mutated the primary's inventory/chest.
  Thread the acting PlayerState through.
- **restore ignored gameMode/gameOver**: `serializePlayer` writes both but
  `restorePlayerFields` never read them, so a rejoining player lost their mode
  (and a dead hardcore player its game-over). Restore them, resolving mode the
  same way the constructor does (game-over → spectator, hardcore → survival).
- **mobs targeted corpses**: `nearestTargetablePlayer` didn't skip dead
  players, so a mob could keep hunting a dead survival player over a nearby
  live one.
- **hardcore game-over hearts reset**: `tickHealthRegen` topped a game-over
  Spectator back to MAX_HEARTS, overwriting the withered hearts=0 that
  triggerGameOver set — guard on `!gameOver`.
- **stuck sleepers on leave**: if the last awake player left while others
  slept, nothing re-ran the sleep gate; recompute it in removePlayer.
- Cap `elapsed` in applyRemotePose (companion to the server's lastPoseTick
  fix) so the pose clamp can't be inflated regardless of caller bugs.

Tests: per-player moveStack isolation, gameMode/gameOver restore, dead-player
target skipping, and hearts staying 0 through a game-over.
EOF
